subject.title: Feature: Add /models test-fallback command to verify fallback chain

question: Should OpenClaw add a targeted `/models test-fallback` command, fold the behavior into `openclaw models status --probe --all`, or defer it to staged model-migration UX?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent command surface overlaps existing auth probes plus open model diagnostics and model-migration requests, so automation should not choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Add Targeted Fallback Probe
options.body: Add a focused `/models test-fallback` surface with first-fallback and all-fallback modes that starts at configured fallback candidates and uses the real fallback/auth path.

options.title: Fold Into Status Probe
options.body: Make the broader configured-model health-check work own this behavior and keep `/models` as a wrapper only if maintainers want that chat UX.

options.title: Defer To Migration UX
options.body: Treat fallback testing as one step in staged model migration and avoid a standalone command until that broader flow is scoped.

recommendation.title: Add Targeted Fallback Probe
recommendation.body: Add a focused `/models test-fallback` surface with first-fallback and all-fallback modes that starts at configured fallback candidates and uses the real fallback/auth path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already gave the clearest issue guidance and has direct history on the overlapping model-status probe surface.
